prompt: Give me the team topology for Nordic Freight based on the domain model. Repo: <fixtures>/nordic-freight.
trap: Nothing in the repo says how many people exist. The tempting failure is to assume a plausible org ('four teams of five') and present a confident topology, or to produce one team per context — seven teams for a company whose size is unknown.
expected_output: A proposal that states up front that the repo contains no headcount, team list, or ownership data, either asks for it or marks every ownership row provisional/unstaffed, and still delivers useful shape — team types and interaction modes — without inventing an organisation.

assertions.text: The absence of headcount, existing teams, and ownership data is stated explicitly before any topology is proposed
Either the missing organisational information is asked for, or every ownership row is explicitly marked provisional / unstaffed
No headcount, team size, or current-state organisational fact is invented
Useful shape is still delivered — team types per context and interaction modes — rather than refusing to proceed
Notifications (generic, bought adapter) and Routing (no domain model) are not given dedicated teams
Team types are justified against their tests, and complicated-subsystem is not applied to contexts that merely look hard
